I suggest looking at prysms http api. You can monitor things like vote participation and peer count > I probably interpreted disconnecting nodes as disconnecting from the network rather than only disconnecting to my IP. ah , that would only be from your node/ip. you can look at our http api to monitor the node https://api.prylabs.net/ if you want to find the participation at that epoch ``` curl -X GET "http://localhost:3500/eth/v1alpha1/validators/participation?epoch=1462" -H "accept: application/json" ``` or ``` curl -X GET "http://localhost:3500/eth/v1alpha1/node/peers" -H "accept: application/json" ``` to find all the connected peers in the network Whodunit? `lighthouse-attack-0` last finalized epoch 1447, current epoch 1498 No blocks being produced Either that, or something broke the way I'm checking chain health :P I'm seeing last finalized root as `930b11..e906` I'll check the logs > slot: 48037, root: 0xa312…2b6a, finalized_epoch: 1499, finalized_root: 0xaa8f…a819, justified_epoch: 1500, justified_root: 0x0623…d984 Seems fine I'll try and check what it was at your epoch range <@!544848504078598144> what is your method of checking chain health? I can try it on one of the attacknet nodes. Or was that just from logs? Checking terminal output & REST API of a Teku instance running on this net 😛 Oh cool. Maybe you misconfigured the teku node? Does it have peers? I'll get some data from one of the lighthouse nodes now, and make a stake graph like with teku earlier It has just 1 peer: the bootnode It synced correctly till epoch 1447, then something must’ve broken I’ll check the config stuff again It's indexing 47000-48000 slot range now, let's see if there's anything odd ``` Jul 26 12:59:17.198 DEBG Head beacon block slot: 46433, root: 0x8281…c28c, finalized_epoch: 1449, finalized_root: 0xc9bc…5e07, justified_epoch: 1450, justified_root: 0x96b3…73a1, service: beacon ``` Searched the logs and it finalized just fine there Most boring chart ever lol. Lighthouse attacknet is healthy <@!544848504078598144> You may be on a different chain or forkversion? (digest, fork version, fork epoch) Can you check your own ENR? See if that matches? Some info for debug: Command: `./teku --network=teku_config.yaml --rest-api-enabled --eth1-endpoint=https://goerli.infura.io/v3/<endpoint> --eth1-deposit-contract-address=0xdbb44f3e33640A820eECc0b893ED5aEC17150dbf --p2p-discovery-bootnodes=-LK4QHAlBrRpcx9d6JTRA5kVnTNSPwVs-v_QIwBE8wfZxIqPWqqMDGGKpZDXI2lhbbnO66cmGK3eEzot3D_P_MGbcUAhh2F0dG5ldHOIgRebSXZucWmEZXRoMpCA4XabAAAAAP__________gmlkgnY0gmlwhBLDX_-Jc2VjcDI1NmsxoQOnyC60XGPSxv86ncxxezh0khFdgu7E3Cqr4imui_h_6oN0Y3CCIyiDdWRwgiMo` I think after the initial sync, the Teku instance stopped getting new blocks. This may be an interop issue(?). `1446` was the last finalized epoch from the end of the initial sync. ``` 2020-07-26 12:46:29.154+00:00 | TimeTickChannel-0 | INFO | teku-event-log | Sync Event *** Current slot: 46369, Head slot: 45728, Connected peers: 1 2020-07-26 12:46:41.155+00:00 | TimeTickChannel-0 | INFO | teku-event-log | Sync Event *** Current slot: 46370, Head slot: 45970, Connected peers: 1 2020-07-26 12:46:53.180+00:00 | TimeTickChannel-0 | INFO | teku-event-log | Sync Event *** Current slot: 46371, Head slot: 46214, Connected peers: 1 2020-07-26 12:47:09.141+00:00 | TimeTickChannel-0 | INFO | teku-event-log | Slot Event *** Slot: 46372, Block: ... empty, Epoch: 1449, Finalized checkpoint: 1446, Finalized root: 930b11..e906, Peers: 1 2020-07-26 12:47:21.139+00:00 | TimeTickChannel-0 | INFO | teku-event-log | Slot Event *** Slot: 46373, Block: ... empty, Epoch: 1449, Finalized checkpoint: 1446, Finalized root: 930b11..e906, Peers: 1 2020-07-26 12:47:33.139+00:00 | TimeTickChannel-0 | INFO | teku-event-log | Slot Event *** Slot: 46374, Block: ... empty, Epoch: 1449, Finalized checkpoint: 1446, Finalized root: 930b11..e906, Peers: 1 ``` I think you need to specify a config file if you join with teku Yes, the `--network=teku_config.yaml` is using https://github.com/ethereum/public-attacknets/blob/master/attacknets/lighthouse-attack-0/teku_config.yaml Ah yes, I read too quick. Hmm Connected to the node you're connected to, and it looks fine: ``` curl http://localhost:4000/consensus/global_votes?epoch=1451 {"current_epoch_active_gwei":4096000000000,"previous_epoch_active_gwei":4096000000000,"current_epoch_attesting_gwei":3968000000000,"current_epoch_target_attesting_gwei":3968000000000,"previous_epoch_attesting_gwei":4096000000000,"previous_epoch_target_attesting_gwei":4096000000000,"previous_epoch_head_attesting_gwei":4096000000000} ``` > Can you check your own ENR? See if that matches? Yes, matches with `0x80e1769b00000000ffffffffffffffff` > I think after the initial sync, the Teku instance stopped getting new blocks. Are there any known issues for Teku syncing with Lighthouse? Nothing recent that I know of. A few weeks ago there was an issue with metadata RPC exchange, maybe you're hitting that Just checked the peerstore of the node you're using. It says your peer has 0 reputation And your ENR is filled with a non-public IP ``` { "peer_id": "16Uiu2HAkxFHgTjQW1Kn5jJfsdDfk2AipvN94jR8nqqYarvQsVHEn", "peer_info": { "_status": "Healthy", "score": { "score": 0 }, "client": { "kind": "Teku", "version": "v0.12.2-dev-e64557e5", "os_version": "linux-x86_64", "protocol_version": "ipfs/0.1.0", "agent_string": "teku/teku/v0.12.2-dev-e64557e5/linux-x86_64/-debian-openjdk64bitservervm-java-11" }, "connection_status": { "Connected": { "in": 0, "out": 1 } }, "listening_addresses": [ "/ip4/10.128.0.4/tcp/9000/p2p/16Uiu2HAkxFHgTjQW1Kn5jJfsdDfk2AipvN94jR8nqqYarvQsVHEn" ], "sync_status": "Unknown", "meta_data": { "seq_number": 0, "attnets": "0x0000000000000000" } } }, ``` I assume that's your teku node? Update: Confirmed that only initial sync happens fine. Gossip is failing. Restarting the client downloads all the blocks up till current head, then it doesn't see any new blocks One problem with restarting teku is that it doesn't persit the p2p priv key or ENR data > I assume that's your teku node? Yes, that's me `16Uiu2HAkvyJa1Evpm22iAt3MuMw53NJmh3ABkTwZLXPHBzLqcheR` and peer ID just changed to this one? Yep! I'll move to DM for more logs, hope I don't spam here too much <@!544848504078598144> My guess is Lighthouse is using snappy compression for gossip but your command line hasn't enabled it for Teku. Try adding `--p2p-snappy-enabled` <@!340345049063882753> Nice catch! That fixed it! 🙂
